"'''All 4 Love'''" is a song by American music group [[Color Me Badd]]. Outside North America, it was released<!-- Do not add the labels here; it creates a run-on sentence --> as second single from their debut album, ''[[C.M.B.]]'' (1991), while in the United States and Canada, it served as the third single. The recording was produced by [[Howie Tee]] and contains elements from the 1966 song "Patch My Heart" by [[the Mad Lads]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stereogum.com/2171560/the-number-ones-color-me-badds-all-4-love/columns/the-number-ones/|title=The Number Ones: Color Me Badd's 'All 4 Love'|last=Breihan|first=Tom|website=[[Stereogum]]|date=December 31, 2021|access-date=January 2, 2022}}</ref>

On the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], the song reached number one on January 25, 1992; it was the band's second and final number-one single in the US. The song also reached number two on the US [[Cash Box Top 100 Pop Singles|''Cash Box'' Top 100]] and topped the [[New Zealand Singles Chart]]. It additionally became a top-10 hit in several other countries.

"All 4 Love" is a song by American music group Color Me Badd. Outside North America, it was released as second single from their debut album, C.M.B. (1991), while in the United States and Canada, it served as the third single. The recording was produced by Howie Tee and contains elements from the 1966 song "Patch My Heart" by the Mad Lads.

On the US Billboard Hot 100, the song reached number one on January 25, 1992; it was the band's second and final number-one single in the US. The song also reached number two on the US Cash Box Top 100 and topped the New Zealand Singles Chart. It additionally became a top-10 hit in several other countries.
